newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: N.Irish foes to meet in S.Africa, mediator says.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish foes to meet in S.Africa, mediator says.

text.p: An Irish academic told Saturday's Star newspaper in Johannesburg that South Africa would be the venue for a conference next week bringing together Northern Ireland's political foes.

Boston-based Padraig O'Malley, who thought up the four-day talks to be held from Thursday at a secret location, said all the province's political parties would attend, including Sinn Fein, political wing of the Irish Republican Army.

"The idea is to get the parties together and discuss how we did things here," said Roelf Meyer who, as chief negotiator for South Africa's last white president F.W. de Klerk, helped smooth the 1994 transition to black majority rule.

His opposite number at the time from President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress, Cyril Ramaphosa, would also take part, O'Malley said, but the South African government would not be playing a mediating role.
He did not say which Northern Irish politicians would attend, but made clear the conference was being structured so that they could avoid sitting down together at the same table if they desired.
The constitutional development ministry which is organising the talks said full details would be issued on Tuesday.
